Done. Memory is at 92% so I'll skip adding to it — the skill reference captures this fully and is the right home for a procedural pattern.

Reflection summary:

Generalizable lesson learned: "In which YEAR did X peak/bottom?" questions over a multi-decade span (personal saving rate, unemployment, CPI, etc.) have a distinct failure mode — off-by-ONE-YEAR. The top candidate years sit on a plateau where adjacent bars are nearly equal height, so eyeballing the tallest bar picks the wrong neighbor. My answer 1974 was adjacent to gold 1973 (both ~10% mid-70s saving-rate years).

What I saved:
- New reference: references/peak-trough-year-from-timeseries.md — procedure to read NUMERIC values not bar heights, compare top candidates side by side, prefer the EARLIER year on a tie, and sanity-check against famous historical peak years (saving rate early-mid 70s, unemployment 82-83, CPI 1980).
- Pointer added in SKILL.md so future runs surface it.

No memory update (already at 92%; this is procedural, not a durable cross-session fact, so it belongs in the skill).
